# Offboarding revocation

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:offboarding` · **Epic:** [#161](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/161) · **Tickets:** 4 (2S 2M)

A CP background job refreshes each user's stored Dex refresh token on a schedule; when Dex refuses it or reports the user disabled, the user is blocked and all their provider grants are revoked and deleted. Admins can also offboard a user manually from the console.

## How we build it

- Job: every consent.offboarding.interval (default 1h, jittered), for each idp_links row refresh at the Dex token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token; store the rotated refresh token back to warden/users/<sub>/_idp; record last_refresh_status.
- Failure classes: invalid_grant (user disabled, deleted or session revoked in the upstream IdP) → offboard; network/5xx → retry with backoff, alert after consent.offboarding.maxFailures (default 3) consecutive transient failures, never offboard on transient errors.
- Offboard(sub, reason): add sub to blockedUsers in the current policy version (p1-block-list) first, then for each grant RevokeUserGrant, then delete warden/users/<sub>/_idp and mark idp_links offboarded; idempotent and resumable.
- Manual: POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard (admin role) with reason; audit user.offboarded with actor, reason and the list of revoked providers; alert routed through internal/alertpipeline.

## Done when

Disabling a user in Dex results, within one job interval, in that user being on the block list, their provider tokens revoked at the provider and their vault entries deleted, with an audit record.

### 1/4 · W-P3-OFFB-01

**Implement idempotent Offboard(sub, reason) operation**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#162](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/162)

Add oauthbroker.Offboard(ctx, sub, reason, actor) that adds sub to blockedUsers via the versioned policy store (new version with author system:offboarding), calls RevokeUserGrant for every active grant, deletes warden/users/<sub>/_idp, and sets idp_links.offboarded_at. Each step is recorded in an offboard_runs row so a crash resumes from the last completed step. Emits audit user.offboarded.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] After Offboard the served policy contains sub in blockedUsers and a worker denies that user
- [ ] All warden/users/<sub>/* keys are deleted and the fake providers saw revoke calls
- [ ] Running Offboard twice is a no-op the second time

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PORT-02`](consent-portal.md#24--w-p3-port-02) Implement revoke: provider revoke, vault delete, worker invalidation

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-OFFB-02`](offboarding.md#24--w-p3-offb-02) Add periodic Dex refresh job with failure classification; [`W-P3-OFFB-03`](offboarding.md#34--w-p3-offb-03) Add manual offboard action to console

### 2/4 · W-P3-OFFB-02

**Add periodic Dex refresh job with failure classification**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#163](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/163)

Add a ticker in controlplane.Server (alongside the retention pruner) running the refresh job per consent.offboarding.interval with per-user jitter and bounded concurrency (consent.offboarding.concurrency, default 4). Use the generic OIDC client's token endpoint; write rotated refresh tokens back with SecretStore.Put. invalid_grant triggers Offboard; transient errors increment a counter and raise an alert at maxFailures.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Fake IdP returning invalid_grant for a user triggers Offboard within one interval
- [ ] A 503 from the IdP never offboards and alerts after 3 consecutive failures
- [ ] A rotated refresh token replaces the stored one

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#14--w-p3-offb-01) Implement idempotent Offboard(sub, reason) operation; [`W-P3-CSIG-03`](consent-auth.md#34--w-p3-csig-03) Store Dex refresh token in the secret backend on login

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-OFFB-04`](offboarding.md#44--w-p3-offb-04) E2E: disable a Dex user and verify full revocation

### 3/4 · W-P3-OFFB-03

**Add manual offboard action to console**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#164](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/164)

Add GET /dashboard/api/users (sub, email, grants count, last_refresh_status) and POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard requiring the admin role and a reason; it calls Offboard with the console user as actor. Add a Users tab to internal/dashboard/index.html with a confirm dialog.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Viewer and editor roles get 403 on the offboard endpoint
- [ ] Admin offboard produces an audit record with actor and reason
- [ ] Users tab shows offboarded users with their offboarded_at time

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#14--w-p3-offb-01) Implement idempotent Offboard(sub, reason) operation

### 4/4 · W-P3-OFFB-04

**E2E: disable a Dex user and verify full revocation**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#165](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/165)

Integration test (build tag) with Dex static password connector replaced by a fake upstream IdP that can disable a user: connect Google via the fake provider, disable the user, run the refresh job once, then assert block list, revoke calls, vault deletion and that the worker denies the user's next request.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Test passes in CI under the integration tag
- [ ] The worker denial reason is user_blocked

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-OFFB-02`](offboarding.md#24--w-p3-offb-02) Add periodic Dex refresh job with failure classification
